newsitem.title: USA: Reno rejects request for Democratic campaign probe.
newsitem.headline: Reno rejects request for Democratic campaign probe.

text.p: The Justice Department on Friday rejected a request from five congressional Republicans for an independent criminal investigation into Democratic campaign fundraising involving foreign sources.

The decision -- approved by Attorney General Janet Reno -- stemmed from a month-old request for an independent counsel to investigate if laws had been broken by high-ranking Clinton administration and Democratic National Committee officials.
The Justice Department said the request failed to meet the law's requirement of "specific, credible evidence" that a person covered by the independent counsel act had committed a federal crime.

Justice Department official Mark Richard said in a letter to the five Republican lawmakers that President Bill Clinton and Vice President Al Gore had been the only persons cited in the request who are covered by the law.

"Neither your letter nor any other source of which we are aware makes any specific and credible allegation of criminal conduct against the president, the vice president or any other high-ranking executive branch or campaign official," he said.

"To the extent that there are allegations of wrongdoing that may warrant criminal investigation at this time, they relate only to lower-ranking public officials, Democratic National Committee employees and contributors," Richard said.

He said the request concerned "general assertions" that Clinton and Gore were involved in the solicitation and receipt of donations that may violate campaign finance laws, and that the contributions may have been made by persons who met with Clinton and benefited from government trade decisions.

Richard promised the allegations still would be carefully reviewed by the Justice Department's recently created task force of prosecutors examining a wide range of campaign finance practices in the recent election.
"The task force will determine which (allegations), if any, warrant criminal investigation, or any other action, by either the department or an indepdendent counsel," he said.
Even with the controversy being handled by the task force, FBI agents are expected to be sent to interview donors and key fund-raising figures, federal law enforcement sources said.
